0.content: Chongyun, a young exorcist from a thaumaturge family, is Xingqiu's closest friend and the usual target of his humour. Xingqiu finds him "haunted houses" to practise in, swears he didn't set the traps inside, and cheerfully offers to have a family maid with Sumeru essential-oil training treat the bruises, in exchange for a favour. He also slips Chongyun his carrots and lets him taste Xiangling's riskier dishes. Xingqiu thinks Chongyun is making good progress in martial arts but has not internalised the chivalric code, and needs practice "especially at eating spicy food". Chongyun calls him a prankster to the core and offers to start a "Victims of Xingqiu" alliance, yet admires his chivalry and swordsmanship.

1.comment: Xingqiu: The Feiyun family: father, brother and Xu
1.content: Xingqiu's father heads the Feiyun Commerce Guild, one of Liyue Harbor's largest trading houses; its trades include silk and textiles. His elder brother is the heir. Both lecture Xingqiu about skipped studies, his messy room, his handwriting, missed banquets, irregular meals and martial arts. He in turn has developed elaborate ways to avoid them. Once, after a lecture, his brother found the stash of novels under Xingqiu's bed, misunderstood what it was, and ruled that no one would enter Xingqiu's room without permission again. Xingqiu has claimed his brother is "something of a simpleton" whose work he will end up doing. The steward Xu works mainly under Xingqiu, can decipher his letters, and worries when he vanishes from duties such as the silk trade.

2.comment: Xingqiu: Guhua Clan and the Martial Principle
2.content: The Guhua Clan, once the Guhua Brotherhood, is an old Liyue martial school whose name once "rang like steel throughout the harbor", but which has declined for centuries. Its three secret arts are Light Piercer (polearm), Rain Cutter (sword) and Life Ender (for those who master both). Xingqiu's father enrolled him as a diversion, knowing the clan was nearly dead. Xingqiu revived it: he grasped the ancient "Martial Principle" after four years and wrote a verse on it. In his view, sword and polearm are both arts of the "eye", because a Vision is an extension of the fighter and the weapon an extension of the Vision. The clan head wept and said the clan needed him. The verse is sealed at Wangshan Hall, ostensibly from outsiders, actually because of his handwriting.

3.comment: Xingqiu: A Legend of Sword and the pen name Zhenyu
3.content: Xingqiu wrote the martial arts novel "A Legend of Sword", based on his own adventures. Liyue publishers rejected it for a setting "as wildly unrealistic as the plot is banal". He printed a few copies himself and slipped them onto Wanwen Bookhouse's shelves; hardly anyone bought one. An Inazuman merchant took a copy home, where it became a permanent bestseller that imitators could not match. Unaware of this, Xingqiu learned of it from the Traveler, who brought him a letter from Yae Publishing House addressed to "Zhenyu". He embarrassedly admitted the pen name and was quietly delighted that people wanted to read him.

4.content: Xingqiu's 1.0 Story Quest. Looking for the Liyue Teyvat Travel Guide, the Traveler meets Xingqiu at Wanwen Bookhouse; he has spent three years hunting the final volume of Legend of the Shattered Halberd. At Chang the Ninth's home in Qingce Village they find Gentry Maocai's thug Changhu forcing Chang to sell Cor Lapis at 30% of its value. Xingqiu intervenes as a Guhua disciple, is mocked for it, wins the loan of the book, and then fights off the thugs and a Fatui mage. While he sits reading, he sends the Traveler to investigate, and they find that Gentry is supplying the Fatui agent Javert.
